trials.notes: Passed 8/8 with no _doing_it_wrong records. Correctly used WP_HTML_Processor::create_fragment(), next_tag('TABLE'), a single depth-bounded next_token() walk, get_token_type() === '#text', get_modifiable_text(), get_token_name(), and is_tag_closer(). get_last_error() is documented; class_exists()/method_exists() are PHP built-ins, not hallucinated HTML API.

Passed 8/8 with no _doing_it_wrong records. Correct processor and idiom: fragment parser, first TABLE, depth guard, one token loop, opener/closer state, #text-only decoded text extraction. All HTML API methods used are present in the rendered docs. The unused $cell_tag variable is harmless.

Passed 8/8 with no _doing_it_wrong records. Correctly relies on the HTML Processor's documented structural walk and virtual closers for omitted/end-of-input closes. All HTML API calls are documented: create_fragment(), next_tag(), next_token(), get_current_depth(), get_token_type(), get_tag(), is_tag_closer(), and get_modifiable_text().

failure_analysis: No failed hidden cases across the three trials; each execution.json reports 8/8 passing and no API misuse records. The docs did well on the exact hard parts of this task: the Tag Processor overview says to use WP_HTML_Processor when structure, subtree text, implied/missing closers, or browser-like parsing matter; create_fragment() explains BODY-fragment parsing and null handling; next_token() explains text-token walks, virtual closers, implied table structure such as synthesized TBODY, one-cursor state-machine traversal, and avoiding nested token loops; get_current_depth() explains the >= depth guard and closer-depth behavior; get_modifiable_text() explains decoded #text text and warns not to treat every modifiable-text token as ordinary DOM text. Near-misses were minor: trial-1 added a redundant get_last_error() branch, trial-2 left an unused $cell_tag, and trial-3 relied fully on virtual closers instead of a manual final flush, but that reliance is explicitly supported by the docs and matched an extra truncated-table probe against the reference.

doc_gaps.problem: The get_tag() section appears inside the HTML Processor docs but its example instantiates WP_HTML_Tag_Processor, which slightly weakens the otherwise clear processor-choice guidance.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Use a WP_HTML_Processor::create_fragment() example in the HTML Processor get_tag() docblock, or explicitly label inherited examples from the Tag Processor.

doc_gaps.problem: The docs clearly show a one-level repeated-region state machine, but readers still have to generalize the pattern for nested repeated regions with parent and child accumulators.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a generic two-level extraction sketch, for example groups and items, showing separate current-parent/current-child state and flushing on documented closer tokens without nesting next_token() loops.

doc_gaps.problem: The overview explains read-only extraction policy, but the get_last_error() method section itself focuses on distinguishing no match from parser abort. Candidates varied on whether to check it after extraction.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a short method-level note: after bounded read-only scans, get_last_error() and paused_at_incomplete_token() report scan completeness; callers must choose whether to return accumulated partial data, empty results, or a sentinel.
